learn.title: Electric Vehicles: Motors & Charging
learn.intro: Electric vehicles (EVs) reduce fossil fuel dependence by converting electricity into motion. Understanding their motors, regenerative braking, and charging is key to adopting cleaner transport.
learn.c1_title: EV Motors: Turning Electricity into Motion 🔋
learn.c1_text: EV motors use electromagnetic fields to convert electricity into rotational energy. Unlike internal combustion engines, they’re 90% efficient, wasting far less energy as heat. This efficiency lets EVs travel farther on a single charge compared to gas-powered cars.
learn.c2_text: Regenerative braking captures kinetic energy during deceleration, converting it into stored electricity. For example, Tesla’s regenerative braking can recover up to 30% of energy typically lost in braking, extending range by 10-15% in city driving.
learn.c3_text: India’s EV charging network expanded to 4,000+ public chargers in 2023, but lags behind China’s 2.8 million. Policies like FAME II aim to install 50,000 chargers nationwide by 2025 to support EV adoption.
learn.stat2: Global EV sales hit 14 million in 2023 (IEA)

learn.title: Hydrogen Colors: Clean vs Dirty
learn.intro: Hydrogen’s color codes reveal its production method. Green hydrogen (renewable-powered) is climate-friendly, while grey and blue hydrogen rely on fossil fuels, impacting emissions.
learn.c1_text: Grey hydrogen, produced via steam methane reforming (SMR), emits 9-10 kg CO2 per kg H2. In 2022, 76 million tons of grey hydrogen were produced globally, contributing 2% of energy-related emissions.
learn.c2_text: Blue hydrogen adds carbon capture to SMR, reducing emissions by 60-70%. However, only 2% of global hydrogen production uses this method due to high costs and technical challenges.
learn.c3_text: India aims to produce 5 million tons of green hydrogen annually by 2030, leveraging 444 GW of renewable capacity. Projects like Gujarat’s 300 MW electrolyzer (2023) target $2/kg H2 by 2025.
learn.stat1: India’s green hydrogen target: 5 M tons/year (2030)

learn.title: Solar PV: Sun to Electricity
learn.intro: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity via the photoelectric effect. This process powers homes and industries, driving the global shift to renewables.
learn.c1_text: When sunlight hits silicon cells, photons knock electrons loose, creating direct current (DC). A 300W panel generates ~1.5 kWh daily in India, enough to power a household fridge for 10 hours.
learn.c2_text: Inverters convert DC from panels to AC for home use. A 5 kW system with a 97% efficient inverter delivers ~4.85 kW AC, powering 15-20 appliances simultaneously.
learn.c3_text: India added 16.7 GW of solar capacity in 2023, reaching 72 GW total. The PM-KUSUM scheme aims to install 10 GW on farm pumps by 2026, reducing diesel use by 1.1 million liters annually.

learn.title: Carbon Markets: Trading Clean Air
learn.intro: Carbon markets let companies buy/sell emission permits, incentivizing clean energy adoption. India’s carbon credit trading platform launched in 2022.
learn.c1_text: One carbon credit equals 1 ton of CO2 reduced. India’s first carbon trading platform, launched in 2022, allows firms to trade permits, with 1.2 million tons traded in its pilot phase.
learn.c2_text: Cap-and-trade sets emission caps, letting companies trade allowances. The EU ETS reduced emissions by 38% since 2005, while India’s 2023 draft rules target 10% emission reductions by 2030.
learn.c3_text: India’s 2022 carbon credit trading pilot involved 12 power plants, with 1.2 million tons traded. The 2023 draft rules aim to expand to 500+ industries by 2025, aligning with net-zero goals.
learn.stat1: India’s carbon credit pilot: 1.2 M tons (2023)

learn.title: Smart Grids: Powering the Future
learn.intro: Smart grids use sensors and AI to optimize electricity flow, integrating renewables and reducing outages. India’s smart grid initiatives aim to cut losses by 15% by 2030.
learn.c1_text: Smart meters track usage hourly, enabling dynamic pricing. In Delhi, pilot projects reduced peak demand by 8% through time-of-use tariffs, saving consumers ₹1,200 annually.
learn.c2_text: AI and IoT sensors detect faults and reroute power. India’s 450 kV grid automation project reduced outage duration by 40% in Rajasthan, saving ₹2,500 crore annually.
learn.c3_text: India plans 100 smart cities with integrated grids by 2030. The 2023 National Smart Grid Mission targets 15% transmission loss reduction, with pilot projects in Gujarat cutting losses by 12% since 2020.
learn.stat1: India’s smart grid target: 15% loss reduction (2030)

learn.title: Bifacial Solar Panels: Double-Sided Power
learn.intro: Bifacial panels capture sunlight on both sides, boosting efficiency by 10-20%. They’re ideal for reflective surfaces like deserts or rooftops.
learn.c1_text: Bifacial panels generate 10-20% more power by absorbing reflected light. A 400W bifacial panel in Rajasthan’s Thar Desert produces 460W annually, outperforming monofacial panels by 15%.
learn.c2_text: Dual-axis trackers tilt panels to follow the sun, increasing bifacial gain. In Gujarat, trackers boosted output by 25%, making bifacial systems 30% more efficient than fixed-tilt setups.
learn.c3_text: India’s 2023 solar tender for 500 MW included 60% bifacial panels. The Bhadla Solar Park uses bifacial modules with 22% efficiency, generating 1.5 GW annually—enough for 500,000 homes.
learn.stat1: India’s bifacial adoption: 60% in 500 MW tender (2023)
